subject: physics_2
question_text: When does an LCR series circuit have minimum impedance?

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Physics hand-checked: Z = √(R² + (ωL − 1/ωC)²); the bracket is the only ω-dependent term, so Z is minimum when ωL = 1/ωC, i.e. at resonance ω = 1/√(LC), leaving Zₘᵢₙ = R and maximum current — matching the book's Zₘᵢₙ = R.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The impedance

ωL is the inductive reactance and 1/ωC is
steps.margin_note: First mark. Write Z in full — the answer reads straight off the bracket.
steps.why: The formula shows the whole answer in advance: R is fixed, and the bracket (ωL − 1/ωC) is the only part that depends on frequency, so Z is smallest when that bracket is zero.
common_mistakes: Writing a plus sign inside the bracket. The two reactances oppose each other, so it is ωL minus 1/ωC.
Adding R and the reactances directly. They add as squares under the root, like the sides of a right triangle.

recall.must_convey: That Z = √(R² + (ωL − 1/ωC)²) for a series LCR circuit.
accept: root of R squared plus the bracket squared
omega L minus 1 by omega C

steps.memory_tip: Impedance triangle: R along the base, (ωL − 1/ωC) upright, Z the longest side.

steps.label: The resonance condition
lines: Z is minimum when the bracket is zero, that
is when ωL = 1/ωC. This is resonance, at
Then Zₘᵢₙ = R and the current in the circuit

lines.text: At resonance ωL = 1/ωC and Zₘᵢₙ = R

steps.margin_note: Second mark. Two things must appear: the condition ωL = 1/ωC and the leftover Zₘᵢₙ = R.
steps.why: At ωL = 1/ωC the two reactances cancel and only R is left, so the circuit draws its largest current — the condition, the frequency and the leftover R together make the full answer.
common_mistakes: Saying the impedance is zero at resonance. The reactances cancel, but R remains: Zₘᵢₙ = R.
Writing ω = √(LC). The resonance angular frequency is 1/√(LC).

recall.must_convey: That Z is minimum at resonance, when ωL = 1/ωC and ω = 1/√(LC), leaving Z = R and maximum current.
accept: omega L equals 1 by omega C
reject: root of R squared plus the bracket squared

steps.memory_tip: Resonance: the L and C parts cancel, R alone is left, the current peaks.

insider_note: Saying at resonance alone is half the answer — the examiner wants the condition ωL = 1/ωC and the leftover Zₘᵢₙ = R.
